This is a crossposting of an unanswered question at stack overflow:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/30325739/ggplot2-for-procrustes-rotation-in-vegan


I want to plot procrustes rotations between to RDA-objects obtained by vegan with ggplot2.

    library(vegan)
    #perform two RDAs, do procrustes:
    pro.test <- procrustes(rda.t1,rda.t2)


I extracted the x,y coordinates from the generated list of class "procrustes" and added a factor "dates".

    test <- data.frame(rda1=pro.test$Yrot[,1], rda2=pro.test$Yrot[,2])
    test$dates <- c(rep("A", 8), rep("B",8), rep("C", 8))
    test.2 <- data.frame(rda1=pro.test$X[,1], rda2=pro.test$X[,2])
    test.2$dates <- c(rep("A", 8), rep("B",8), rep("C", 8))

Now the basic plot:

    ggplot() +
    geom_point(data=test, aes(x=rda1, y=rda2, color=dates)) +
    geom_point(data=test.2,aes(x=rda1, y=rda2, color=dates))

The part i cannot do is the plotting of small lines between each corresponding point in test and test.2
Vegan does plot these rotations with arrows rather than connected points. However, vegan does not khow to color according to sampling groups/factors, which is important for me.
Having arrows in the ggplot would be extremely great - i know there is a geom_segment with the argument "arrow".

Could you help me?

Hi,

I've had a go at this, but don't want to install the library
and have no idea what a procrustes is, so I may have gotten
hold of the wrong end of the stick.

> I extracted the x,y coordinates from the generated list of class
> "procrustes" and added a factor "dates".
>
> test <- data.frame(rda1=pro.test$Yrot[,1], rda2=pro.test$Yrot[,2])
> test$dates <- c(rep("A", 8), rep("B",8), rep("C", 8))
> test.2 <- data.frame(rda1=pro.test$X[,1], rda2=pro.test$X[,2])
> test.2$dates <- c(rep("A", 8), rep("B",8), rep("C", 8))
>
> Now the basic plot:
>
> ggplot() +
> geom_point(data=test, aes(x=rda1, y=rda2, color=dates)) +
> geom_point(data=test.2,aes(x=rda1, y=rda2, color=dates))
>
> The part i cannot do is the plotting of small lines between each
> corresponding point in test and test.2
> Vegan does plot these rotations with arrows rather than connected
> points. However, vegan does not khow to color according to sampling
> groups/factors, which is important for me.
> Having arrows in the ggplot would be extremely great - i know there is a
> geom_segment with the argument "arrow".
>
> Could you help me?

# geom_segment needs start end end points on the same row so...
ctest <- data.frame(rda1=pro.test$Yrot[,1],
rda2=pro.test$Yrot[,2],xrda1=pro.test$X[,1],
xrda2=pro.test$X[,2],dates=rep(c("A","B","C"),each=8))

# (nb, without vegan I couldn't use your dput output as it was
# looking for a procrustes function - I grabbed the Yrot and X
# bits out of it. Hopefully correctly, or at least well enough to
# let me answer the question right).


ggplot(ctest) +
geom_point(aes(x=rda1, y=rda2, colour=dates)) +
geom_point(aes(x=xrda1, y=xrda2, colour=dates)) +
geom_segment(aes(x=rda1,y=rda2,xend=xrda1,yend=xrda2,colour=dates),arrow=arrow(length=unit(0.2,"cm")))

Does this do what you want, or have I misunderstood the question?

Ron.

parts:
Thank you very much!!

I exchanged rda1/2 and xrda1/2, also left out the endpoints (as the arrow ends are already indicating where the points end up), and added inner axes,
so the final plot was achieved with:

ggplot(ctest) +
  geom_point(aes(x=xrda1, y=xrda2, colour=dates)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x=xrda1,y=xrda2,xend=rda1,yend=rda2,colour=dates),arrow=arrow(length=unit(0.2,"cm"))) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope=0, linetype=4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, slope=0, linetype=4) +
  theme_bw()
